title: Academy Evaluations Hub
tagline: Evaluations and attendance hub integrated with the GPS platform

simple.tagline: Assessment and attendance calendar, without anyone typing the same thing twice.
simple.summary: The assessment calendar and attendance tracking lived scattered across six departments. I built a hub that shows the day, week and month in one place. The part that saves the most time: it automatically pulls the data the GPS dashboard already processed, so nobody has to type the same information twice. Over a hundred athletes synced.

problem: Evaluation calendars, attendance and compliance for 6 departments were scattered — and the new hub had to consume GPS/wellness data already processed by the existing platform without duplicating pipelines or creating a second write source.
targetUser: Academy technical staff and departments (U15/U17 categories).
myRole: Sole developer: data modeling, API, UI and integration.
process: Implemented a full-stack Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind app with Drizzle ORM. Two persistence implementations behind per-domain facades (calendar, players, evaluations, compliance): SQLite for local development, managed PostgreSQL for production — switched by a single environment variable. Integration runs through a shared database: the hub reads sessions and wellness read-only; the GPS platform remains the only writer of that data.
keyDecisions: Single writer per data domain: GPS and wellness belong to the existing pipeline; the hub only writes evaluations and calendar, in its own prefixed tables.
Per-domain facades: the same UI and API run on SQLite or the managed database with no code changes.
Canonical athlete name shared across systems — the entire integration depends on that convention.
Calendar with chained blocks (one event per date + category) and 4-state attendance.
result: MVP and integration implemented: day panel, month/week calendar, athlete profile with an integrated GPS + wellness panel, weekly compliance per area, per-department CSV import, and athlete sync from the GPS platform registry — a hundred-plus athletes synced.
learned: Integrating two systems through one database only works with explicit ownership rules — who writes what, and a shared identity key defined before any code. Environment boundaries matter as well: one production variable dropped into the neighbor system's .env broke its local development — the rule is now documented in the file itself.
